New Horizons is doing a lot more than just taking pretty pictures. There are seven instruments on board that you can read about here. Of course, the news is dominated by the pictures that NH is sending back, but that's just what's most interesting to the general public. I'm not going to comment on what the instruments are doing, but there's one in particular that I think is interesting - the Venetia Burney Student Dust Counter (SDC). This thing was built by undergraduates. And I think this illustrates what space exploration does better than anything else - it gets people, especially young people, involved in and excited about science. Why does that matter? The US is losing its dominance in science to other countries. Depending on who you talk to, it's already happened. Big projects like this help to inspire the next generation of American scientists. I don't think you can put a price tag on that.

And regarding the cost... $700M sounds like a lot. But consider that this project has been running for about 15 years. That $45M is nothing compared to the trillions of dollars the federal government spends every year, or the trillions we've spent on war during that same time. I might be wrong, but I think people have a better grasp of what a million dollars is - what it takes to earn it, how much you could buy with it, etc. But a trillion dollars is just an imaginary amount that has no real value. So when they hear we spent hundreds of millions of dollars on something, it's almost more shocking than a trillion dollars. I could be wrong though.

The UFC website used to royally suck. It's still got a ways to go, but since Fight Pass was launched it's improved leaps and bounds. The change that's benefited me the most, so far, has been the Rewards page. If you sign up, you can collect points monthly and use it to pay for Fight Pass. $10/monthly is great deal for the library and live events; but if they give me a way to avoid paying (and all I have to do is visit their site/post on Twitter) I'm all for it.

There are a few ways to earn points and it takes 1000 monthly for FightPass. I'm trying to map them all out and see if it's possible to keep Fight Pass free indefinitely.

  • 50 points - Link a Facebook account - 1x Lifetime
  • 50 points - Link a Twitter account - 1x Lifetime
  • 50 points - Link an Instagram account - 1x Lifetime
  • 50 points - Link a Facebook account - 1x Lifetime
  • 10 points - Continue following UFC on twitter - 1x Monthly
  • 10 points - Continue following UFC on twitter - 1x Monthly
  • 5 points - Visit UFC.com - 1x daily
  • 5 points - Daily Log-in - 1x daily
  • 5 points - Quick Vote - 1x daily, 3x weekly
  • 5 points - Read News Articles - 3x daily
  • 5 points - Watch Videos - 2x daily
  • 10 points - Create or Join a UFC Fantasy Pick’Em League - 1x MONTHLY
  • 10 points - Make picks in a UFC Fantasy Pick’Em League - 1x MONTHLY
  • 10 points - Retweet UFC tweets - 2x daily
  • 10 points - Read the UFC Newsletter email - 5x MONTHLY
  • 10 points - Click links in the UFC Newsletter email - 5x MONTHLY

There are more ways to earn points on a monthly basis (without actually spending money), but they are not explicitly stated on https://www.ufcrewards.com/earn. I will update when I have more information. For now, it appears that if you do every daily action for a 30-day month, you will earn: 1,250 points.

Admittedly, it's quite a few steps and does require daily participation, but I was going to visit UFC.com anyway.
Free Fight Pass with UFC Rewards
